en.title: Exclusive Execution Time of Single-Threaded Functions
en.description:
Given the actual call log of a single thread, compute the exclusive time of each function summed over all its calls. A start log takes over the CPU at the beginning of that second, an end log includes that second, and after a return the previous call resumes; recursion is allowed.

The standard input/output format was compiled by this site; added numeric bounds and the encoding for no-solution cases are explicitly marked and do not claim to be the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n m, followed by m lines of id:start/end:timestamp. 1≤n≤100, 1≤m≤500, each ID is in 0..n−1, and times are 0..1000 and non-decreasing; start times are distinct, end times are distinct, and every start has an end. The log represents a valid call-stack execution: a paused call cannot end first.
en.output: Output n integers, for ID 0 through ID n−1 in order.
hints: Maintain the call stack and the last settled time; on a start, credit the old stack top up to just before t; on an end, credit the current function up to t and set the next time to t+1.
